finding.topic: The observation endpoint signed for EP-3 (DUT pin INT via PA0_PC3_ACM ch15) is not the pad that carries the DTEST0 signal driven by the binding register delta; the observable toggle of a2d_vac2_prst is on the DTEST0 pad = nQON.
finding.consequence: A method contract that captures the toggle on the signed INT_PA0 node (S5_ACM200_FH15/SH15, pull-up K103+K128) would probe a node that the mux registers do not drive: DMUX_EN=1 / DMUX_SEL=21 route a2d_vac2_prst to the DTEST0 output, and DTEST0 is a pad function of nQON. No toggle would be captured, so Rise/Fall/Hys could not be measured at all. Limits, trigger polarity and sampling cannot repair a wrong observation node.
finding.whyThisRoleCannotResolveIt: Swapping the observation node changes a source table, a channel, a route and a relay/pull-up set. Per this role contract (test-method-expert.md lines 3, 10) and the strategy handoff returnRule, source/route/relay/pull-up choices are owned by test-strategy-architect and must not be changed silently by this stage.
finding.triggerThatTheSignedContractItselfDeclar: strategy contract conflicts.CF-4 (lines 754-755): "If the test-method or review stage obtains current-project evidence that the DTEST0 output is physically presented on the nQON pin, the monitor route and its pull-up must be switched together by returning a routed finding to test-strategy-architect; the register delta and the monitor intent are unaffected."
finding.evidenceObtainedByThisStage: Five independent current-project sources (project TestIO workbook dump, the DTEST0 mux table, the project regression code for this very item, the active relay standard for this item family, and the user-confirmed project pad mapping) agree that the DTEST0 output is presented on the nQON pad, and the netlist proves INT_PA0 and nQON are two different DUT Kelvin contacts. This is the trigger condition of CF-4, not a mere open question: it is evidence AGAINST the selected route.
